summary: 1928 Aermotor fire tower on Spruce Mountain in Corinth, manned until 1988, restored and opened in 2015; the tower is closed for structural concerns and the trail closes in hunting season.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives the summit as 2,031 ft (619 m), which is the brief's value. The DEC bulletin gives a 2005 ft summit, and Wikipedia gives 2,005 ft (611 m). The sources disagree, so the story gives no summit figure. The editor should decide before any elevation is published.

The DEC bulletin, dated October 2015, says the tower and trail are open, and Saratoga PLAN says the restoration was completed in September 2015. The SummitPost banner gives September 2016. The story uses 2015 and notes the banner.
DEC gives a 2.4-mile round trip and Saratoga PLAN calls it a 2.5-mile hike. The story uses DEC's figure.

notes_for_editor: The historical record (1928 build, 1988 last staffing, 2014-2015 restoration) is consistent across DEC, NHLR, Saratoga PLAN and SummitPost. The current closure of the tower comes from a Saratoga PLAN page that cites DEC; no date for the structural closure was found, so re-check before publishing. The brief's staffing and access fields were unknown; the 2017 NHLR visit reports say unstaffed. Wikipedia says the tower is one of only 23 remaining in the Adirondacks, and Saratoga PLAN says the park has 25 mountains with towers; neither is used. No notable fire was found in these sources.
